w:r.w:t: Token Ops Challenge — costs we assumed

Sonnet 4.6 is only the starting public-cloud price. The inventory has four models. Each scenario starts on Sonnet while the switch is off, then moves to an open model on a Lenovo machine. After that move, the bill is the machine, not a Sonnet token price.

These are the prices the three scenarios were built on. Prices were read on 6 November 2026. A blended token price is 3 input tokens to 1 output token. A month on the rental card is 730 hours. The cloud line is tokens in the month divided by 1,000,000, times $6.
$3 in, $15 out, $6 blended per million tokens
The cloud line at the start of all three
$0.59 in, $0.79 out, $0.64 blended per million tokens
The open model Brightsky moves to. The slide bill is the servers, not this token rate
No token price. The bill is the H200 server
The open model for the super agent and for claims, hosted in-house
$0.05 in, $0.08 out, $0.06 blended per million tokens
Kept for the small knob. These three scenarios do not use it
The 70B and 8B prices are the Groq row on those OpenRouter pages. The same pages also show cheaper hosts. The 8B headline there is $0.02 in and $0.04 out. The 70B headline is $0.10 in and $0.32 out.

Lenovo sells the server. Lenovo does not publish the monthly figure. The monthly figure is the CoreWeave rental card, used as the booth cost. None of these models call a China API. The Llama rows are Meta open weights for self-hosting.
The chats start on Sonnet in the public cloud, with one H100 server already owned, then move to Llama 3.3 70B on two H100 servers.
Public cloud, plus 1 idle H100 server at $30K

$60K is 2 × $30K. The slide already shows $60K, 75%, and 4×. The one change is the Measure line under $0.06: "down from $0.21" becomes "down from $0.24". $0.21 was the $210K cloud slice only. The full start is $240K.
The tasks start on Sonnet in the public cloud, with five H100 servers already in the bill, then stay on a large model by moving to Llama 3.1 405B on H200 servers.

The large model stays, so this does not drop to 70B. Six H200 servers are 6 × $37K = $222K. The slide already shows $225K, 63%, and 2.7×. The one change is the Measure line under $0.45: "down from $0.90" becomes "down from $1.20". $0.90 was the $450K cloud slice only. The full start is $600K.
The claims start on Sonnet in the public cloud, with one H200 server already owned and the switch off, then move to Llama 3.1 405B on that same server.
Public cloud, plus 1 idle H200 server

The slide still shows $180K + $25K = $205K, then $34K. $25K and $34K are not the H200 price. Change the Off screen to cloud $120K, factory $37K, bill $157K, and $1.57 per claim. Change the Measure screen to a start of $157K, a setup of $37K, $0.37 per claim, down from $1.57, a 76% cut, and 4.2×.
The coding agent starts on Sonnet in the public cloud, with a ThinkStation PGX already at the desk and the switch off, and it stays on that same PGX.
Public cloud, plus PGX at the desk

The slide already shows $150K + $4K = $154K, then $0.62 a request. Leave those figures as they are. The earlier idea of moving the win to a 2× H100 server at $6K is dropped. The $4K line “PGX at the desk” stays an open question. A public listing shows the PGX at $5,859 to buy, not $4,000 a month. Links:
$0.21, $0.90, and $1.80 on the slides are the cloud slice alone. The inventory "down from" price is the full starting bill, cloud plus the machine.
